History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult male with 4-day history of sore throat, nasal congestion, emerging dry cough, and systemic viral symptoms—clinical picture consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza‐like illness.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Under the weather” × 4 days.  
• Timeline:  
  – Day 1–2: Painful sore throat, runny nose, fever; painful swallowing.  
  – Day 3: Sore throat improving; persistent nasal congestion; onset of night sweats, myalgias, headaches.  
  – Day 4 (today): New constant dry cough; mild exertional dyspnea; afebrile after antipyretics.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Paracetamol & Ibuprofen relieve fever/pain.  
• Associated symptoms: Night sweats, generalized headaches (intermittent), myalgias, decreased appetite, increased oral fluid intake, fatigue.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no rest dyspnea, no ear pain/discharge, no visual changes, no photophobia, no nausea/vomiting, bowels & urine normal, no skin rash.

Past Medical History:
• Denies chronic medical conditions.

Medications:
• Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone; works as an accountant.  
• Tobacco: Occasional cigars at company events.  
• Alcohol: Occasional, social.  
• Drugs: Denies.  
• Current work stress described as “manageable”; mood unaffected.

Family History:
• Maternal grandmother – type 2 diabetes.  
• Great-grandfather – eczema.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General / HEENT / Respiratory / CVS / Abdomen / Neuro / Skin: Not recorded (telephone consultation).

Investigations:
• None ordered or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection (probable early influenza-like illness) with resolving fever, emerging dry cough, and systemic symptoms.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Viral URTI/common cold – classic sequence of sore throat → nasal symptoms → cough; self-limited course expected.  
2. Influenza-like illness – systemic symptoms (fever, myalgia, headaches, night sweats) support; short duration so far; no severe features requiring antivirals.  
(No conflicting DDx data provided.)

Issue 1 – Acute Viral Upper Respiratory Infection:
• Education that illness is likely viral and self-limiting (7–10 days expected).  
• Symptomatic care: continue Paracetamol and Ibuprofen as needed (per package directions).  
• Encourage rest, hydration, and temporary absence from work (1–2 days).  
• Warn of red-flags: high or persistent fever, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, purulent sputum, or symptoms > 1 week—seek review sooner if these occur.

Issue 2 – Exertional Dyspnea & Cough:
• Currently mild, occurs only with exertion, no chest pain—monitor.  
• Advise gradual return to normal activity after symptom resolution.  
• Return visit if dyspnea at rest or cough becomes productive/bloody.

Issue 3 – General Health & Prevention:
• Smoking: discuss avoidance of cigar use until recovery; offer smoking cessation resources if desired.  
• Flu prevention: consider annual influenza vaccination (not addressed today).  
• Workplace stress: reassure availability for mental-health support if needed.

General Plan Items:
• Follow-up: Routine re-evaluation in 1 week if not improving; earlier if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• No antibiotics indicated at present.
